To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the electrochemical HOMOs of the meso,mesa-linked diporphyrins are more separated than the corresponding triply-fused diporphyrins, (ii) the presence of a ZnII ion in the meso,mesi-linked diporphyrin array increases the electrochemical H-L gap by 0.3 V, whereas the presence of a CuII ion decreases the electrochemical H–L gap by 0,3 V, and (iii)

(i) the electronic communication in the triply fused and meso,mesolinked diporphyrin systems is different; (ii) the nature of the metal ions bound to the porphyrinic macrocycles strongly affects the electronic communication between the two porphyrin subunits; (iii) the peripheral cyano groups have a strong impact on the redox properties of the triply fused diporhyrins; and (iv) the redox properties in both series of

(i) meso-3-Cyano- and meso- 3,5-dicyanophenyl-substituted porphyrins can be used as building blocks for the construction of novel triply fused dipor-phyrins, (ii) the electrochemical HOMOs and LUMOs in these diporphyrin systems are delocalized over both por-phyrin units and (iii) the electronic communication is strongly influenced by the choice of metal ions
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of novel, triply fused, diporphyrin compounds with mixed‐metal coordination.
the development of novel porphyrin architectures and the study of their properties.
the synthesis of new diporphyrin systems, their structural and spectroscopic characterization, and the electrochemical investigation of electronic communication in the porphyrins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the meso,mesocoupling of the diporphyrins has a much larger effect on the redox behavior than the triply fused diporphyins.
the electronic communication in the triply fused diporphy-rins is much more sensitive to the nature of the metal ion than in the corresponding meso,mes-o-linked derivatives.
the electronic communication between the two porphyrin moieties in the triply fused dipyrrole arrays is stronger than in the meso,mesobridged diporphyrins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to demonstrate that the electrochemical properties of porphyrins can be tuned over a broad range by varying the number of metal ions bound to the macrocycle and the mode of connection.
the electrochemical HOMOs and LUMOs of these diporphyrins can be tuned by the choice of metal ions and the number of cyanophenyl substituents.
we have developed a new synthetic strategy for the preparation of triply fused dipyrrolic macrocycles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electronic communication between the two porphyrin units in a meso, meso-linked diporphyrin can be tuned by the choice of metal ions in a way that is different from the communication in a triply fused diporpyrin.
the electronic communication in the triply fused diporpyrin is much better than that in the meso-meso linked one.
the meso, meso-linked and triply fused dipyrrolic arrays can be used as a platform for the construction of a wide variety of metalloporphyrin architectures.
